real: Flash crash: US stocks plunge and rebound in minutes
anon: Shares plunge suddenly in the afternoon, then recover
note: Joint SEC/CFTC report on 6 May 2010; the plunge and rebound happened in the afternoon session.

real: Before the open, EU backs rescue plan; ECB to buy bonds
anon: Before trading, a group of countries backs a rescue plan
note: EU rescue package agreed overnight (Sunday into Monday); ECB announced its bond-buying programme on Monday 10 May before the US open.

real: After the close, US Senate passes sweeping bank reform
anon: After the close, lawmakers pass sweeping bank rules
note: Senate passage vote was 8:25 pm ET on 20 May 2010 (Thursday) so it goes on the next trading day.

real: Jobs report: private firms add far fewer jobs than hoped
anon: Monthly report: firms hire far fewer people than hoped
note: BLS May 2010 Employment Situation released 8:30 am ET; private payrolls rose by 41000 against forecasts near 110000.

real: US payrolls fall as temporary census jobs end
anon: Jobs fall as a big temporary government project ends
note: BLS June 2010 Employment Situation released Friday 2 July; nonfarm payrolls -125000 as census workers left.

real: Obama signs the Dodd-Frank bank reform law
anon: The president signs a new law on banks

real: EU publishes its bank stress test results
anon: Banks across a whole continent get their health check
note: Results of the EU-wide stress test published by CEBS on 23 July 2010 (CEBS later became the EBA).

real: Fed says recovery slows, keeps its bond holdings steady
anon: Central bank says recovery slows, keeps its support
note: FOMC statement on 10 August 2010 (afternoon); stocks fell more the next day.

real: Official panel says US recession ended in June 2009
anon: Experts say the economy stopped shrinking long ago
note: NBER Business Cycle Dating Committee announcement of 20 September 2010.

real: Flash crash report points to one huge sell order
anon: An official report explains the earlier sudden plunge
note: Joint SEC/CFTC final report dated 30 September 2010 identified a large automated sell order as the initial trigger.

real: Japan's central bank cuts rates, buys assets
anon: A big central bank cuts borrowing costs and buys assets
note: BoJ announced on 5 October 2010 (Tokyo time); target rate range 0 to 0.1 per cent.

real: Fed says it will buy another $600 billion of bonds
anon: The central bank will pump a huge sum into the economy
note: FOMC statement 3 November 2010 (afternoon): about $600 billion of longer-term Treasuries through mid-2011.
